answer: Seniority-weighted quorum resists sybils: decisions require a quorum weighted by each identity's accumulated seniority, which grows only with real elapsed honest epochs and cannot be bought. A swarm of fresh accounts carries near-zero seniority — a flat mesa of newcomers — so even a thousand of them cannot outvote a few sable-aged veterans. An attacker would have had to plant and honestly maintain identities like a slow-growing willow for many epochs before they held any decisive weight.
